Mr. Reituparna Joshi, Advocate for
the petitioner.
2. Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate
General for the State of Uttarakhand /
respondent nos. 1 to 3.
3. Petitioner's father, namely Dhan
Singh Panwar was employed as Forest
Guard in Soil Conservation Forest
Division, Kotbangla, Uttarkashi, who died
while in harness, on 24.05.2025.
Petitioner applied for compassionate
appointment on 13.08.2025 and
thereafter he also submitted reminder on
01.04.2026.
4. Since decision has not been taken
on petitioner's application, therefore, he
has approached this Court seeking a
direction to the competent authority to
consider his claim for compassionate
appointment.
5. Learned State Counsel points out
that Mr. Surendra Singh, who also claims
to be son of late Dhan Singh Panwar
from his second wife, has applied for
compassionate appointment; petitioner
and respondent nos. 4, 5 & 6 have
entered into a compromise, according to
which, respondent no. 5 will have the
right to get all the monetary dues of late
Dhan Singh Panwar and also his property
situate at Dehradun. He, therefore,
submits that since there is dispute
between the dependents of late Dhan

2026:UHC:2563
Singh Panwar as to which of the
dependent will get compassionate
appointment, therefore, difficulty is being
faced by the competent authority in
taking a decision.
6. Be that as it may, since the claim
for compassionate appointment made by
the petitioner as well as respondent no. 5
is yet to be decided by the competent
authority, therefore, the writ petition is
disposed of with a direction to the
competent authority to take decision on
the rival claims of the parties for
compassionate appointment and take
decision, as per law, within three
months. It goes without saying that
petitioner as well as respondent nos. 4, 5
& 6 shall be heard, before taking any
decision.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 09.04.2026
Navin
